candidates.title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis
candidates.authors: Yu H, Hu Z, Tan Q, Wang C, Wang B, Yan Y, Yu Y, Zhang F, Zhang M, Huang Y, Cai D, Wang Y, Zhou H, Wang D, Cheng W
candidates.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

candidates.title: Efficient Propranolol Delivery Enabled by Manganese‐Based Bioactive Metal–Organic Frameworks With High Loading Capacity
candidates.authors: Borhanipasvisheh H, Deghani Siyahaki S, Gholamhosseinzadeh E
candidates.abstract: A green and efficient method was developed for propranolol delivery utilizing manganese‐based bioactive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as biocompatible drug carriers. Mn‐based bioactive MOFs with a high aspect ratio were synthesized and characterized for size (average, 17 µm), morphology, stability, elemental composition, crystallinity, functionality, charge character, and biocompatibility (a protein adsorption capacity of 0.03 µg µg−1 (5 h) and a hemolysis ratio of < 0.5%). Afterward, the MOFs were utilized for drug loading via an encapsulation method, and the drug release studies were also performed. The drug loading was confirmed using the zeta potential, CHN analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) measurements. An encapsulation efficiency of 96% (0.5 W/W (drug/MOFs)) and a maximal capacity (Q max) of 0.526 mg mg−1 were obtained. The drug release showed that 93.72% of the loaded drug was released after 10 h for a composite of 0.25 W/W (drug/MOFs), while for 0.5 W/W (drug/MOFs), the drug release reached a plateau after 3 h. The kinetic studies showed longer release times and higher release rates for higher drug loading efficiency. Overall, herein, a bioactive platform for efficient delivery of propranolol was developed to improve the therapeutic efficacy by enhancing the drug loading and achieving controlled drug release.

candidates.title: Evolutionary Dynamics and Transboundary Spread of Senecavirus A: The Role of Recombination and Global Swine Trade
candidates.authors: Li Y, Cui Y, Gao X, Ji Y, Zeng P, Li S, Chen J, Hui P, Zhou J, Wang D, Wan J, Ma F, Hou L, Liu J
candidates.abstract: Senecavirus A (SVA) is an emerging swine pathogen associated with vesicular disease and neonatal mortality, posing significant challenges to global swine health. Here, we report the isolation and identification of two contemporary SVA strains, JS01 and JS02, from clinically suspected cases in China. Both isolates demonstrated high replication competence and clustered within Clade Ib, the dominant globally circulating swine‐associated lineage, showing close genetic ties to strains from southeastern China. Phylogenetic and recombination analyses identified multiple putative recombination events within nonstructural genomic regions, suggesting that recombination drives SVA diversification. Spatiotemporal analysis revealed uneven sequence availability over time and across regions, with sampling concentrated in Asia and the Americas during 2015–2018. Phylogeographic reconstruction indicated supported geographic transition connecting Brazil to China, the United States, and Canada. Notably, the inferred dispersal pattern visually overlapped with global live‐swine trade networks, pointing to a potential possible link with animal trade. Furthermore, our analysis uncovered a divergent, marine‐associated lineage (Clade II) comprising Senecavirus‐like sequences from dolphins, which represents a distinct sister clade to terrestrial swine‐associated viruses. These findings highlight the evolutionary complexity of SVA and emphasize the importance of genomic surveillance for investigating viral dispersal and its relationship with animal movements.

candidates.title: From GROMACS Molecular Dynamics Simulations to Electronic Absorption Spectra: A Tutorial for Small Molecules in Organic Solvents
candidates.authors: Picarelli C, Raffaini G, Tommasini M
candidates.abstract: Classical molecular dynamics is a theoretical method useful for investigating noncovalent intermolecular interactions and conformational flexibility, enabling the simulation of processes such as aggregation/dissolution and adsorption. Molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry are increasingly introduced in chemistry curricula, yet students may encounter difficulties when translating theoretical concepts into robust simulation protocols, particularly outside biomolecular systems. Here, we present a tutorial designed to guide students through the preparation, execution, and analysis of the simulations of small organic molecules in nonaqueous solvents, followed by the calculation of ultraviolet–visible (UV–vis) absorption spectra using time-dependent density functional theory. This tutorial focuses on several practical issues: obtaining force-field parameters, building simulation cells, selecting ensembles, and interpreting critical simulation parameters. Custom solvent models are validated against reference density and radial distribution functions, demonstrating how selected observables can be used to assess simulation reliability. We illustrate the usefulness of molecular dynamics by showing that molecular flexibility and solvent interactions broaden the UV–vis absorption band of indigo in chloroform. This contribution is intended as a hands-on educational resource for upper-level undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in physical chemistry and computational chemistry courses, as well as for Ph.D. students working in chemistry, physics, or material science, who are approaching molecular simulations. To support dissemination, we have released a ready-to-use package on GitHub that includes solvent boxes and all the necessary files and data for incorporating new molecules into GROMACS simulations: https://github.com/cippee/SolventSafari-for-GROMACS.

candidates.title: GSNO-functionalized hydroxyapatite nanofertilizer for prolonged delivery, detoxification, and yield improvement in maize
candidates.authors: Lee DS, Yoon HY, Kumar Das A, Kang JS, Mun BG, Hussain A, Lee IJ, Jeon JR, Yun BW
candidates.abstract: The agricultural use of nitric oxide (NO) is restricted by the instability of conventional donors. Here, we develop a facile one-pot method to immobilize S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) onto humic acid-coated hydroxyapatite nanoparticles (GSNO-HAs-Fe-HAP NPs). Particle characterization confirms favorable properties for agricultural applications, including prolonged NO release (>6 days) and the mitigation of maize cadmium (Cd) stress. Release test verifies the corelease of humic acid and crop nutrients, while confocal microscopy demonstrates robust NP uptake in maize. Under Cd stress, GSNO-HAs-Fe-HAP outperforms commercial NPK fertilizer, improving photosynthetic efficiency and agronomic traits, reducing grain Cd accumulation by 86%, and upregulating phytochelatins, S-nitrosothiols, and metal transporters (ZmPCR, ZmABCC1, and ZmABCG40). The NP composite reduces ROS accumulation and enhances antioxidant enzyme activity, osmolytes, phenolics, flavonoids, and stress phytohormones. Furthermore, NPs significantly improve soil health parameters and the rhizosphere microbiome. Thus, GSNO-HAs-Fe-HAP is a promising nanofertilizer for prolonged NO delivery and Cd stress mitigation.

candidates.title: Gene prioritization across ancestries uncovers distinct molecular pathophysiology and therapeutic landscape in polycystic ovary syndrome
candidates.authors: Rajavelu S, De D
candidates.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a highly prevalent and heterogeneous endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age, with substantial reproductive, metabolic, and long-term health consequences. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified multiple PCOS-associated loci across diverse populations, the functional interpretation of these predominantly non-coding variants and their translation into clinically actionable targets remain unresolved. Here, we present an integrative population-aware framework that systematically combines regulatory functional genomics, long-range chromatin interactions, genome-wide quantitative trait loci, and protein–protein interaction networks to prioritize effector genes underlying PCOS susceptibility. Applying this framework to East Asian and European populations, we demonstrate robust performance relative to existing approaches and uncover both shared and population-specific functions. Notably, our analyses reveal a predominant enrichment of metabolic dysregulation–associated pathways in East Asian PCOS, whereas European PCOS exhibits a stronger inflammatory and immune-related signature. These population-specific molecular phenotypes were further supported by transcriptomic data from PCOS patient samples. Importantly, integration of genetic evidence with a network-based approach enabled the identification of druggable targets lacking direct genetic cues. Collectively, our study provides mechanistic insight into the ethnic heterogeneity of PCOS and establishes a scalable strategy for genetically informed, population-specific therapeutic prioritization, advancing precision medicine approaches for women’s health.

candidates.title: Green synthesis of copper oxide using Litchi chinensis leaf extract and nanocomposite formation with MXene for antimicrobial and antinematicidal activity
candidates.authors: Zameer R, Rehman W, Rasheed L, Farghaly TA, Shakeel M, Sajid M, Alzahrani AYA
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to develop an eco-friendly CuO-loaded Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposite using Litchi chinensis leaf extract and evaluate its potential for antimicrobial and antinematicidal applications. The objective was to employ a green synthesis strategy in which the leaf extract served as a natural reducing, stabilizing, and capping agent for CuO nanoparticle formation, while Ti3C2Tx MXene was prepared from Ti3AlC2 through chemical etching. The CuO/MXene nanocomposite was fabricated by dispersing CuO nanoparticles with MXene to obtain a hybrid material with improved physicochemical and biological performance. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of plant-derived functional groups and Cu–O bonding, indicating the successful formation and surface stabilization of CuO nanoparticles. XRD confirmed the crystalline nature of CuO; SEM showed CuO nanoparticles ranging from 82.82–147.53 nm, MXene sheets around 696.04–740.39 nm, and CuO/MXene particles between 118.03 and 134.37 nm. TGA showed high thermal stability with residues of 88.7% for CuO, 93.5% for MXene, and 85.22% for CuO/MXene. Antibacterial results showed inhibition zones of 11 mm for CuO against S. aureus and 8 mm against E. coli, while CuO/MXene showed 8 mm and 7 mm, respectively. Antinematicidal activity against C. elegans reached 45.67% for CuO, 67.67% for MXene, and 63% for CuO/MXene at 100 µg µl−1. Overall, the study revealed that the synthesized nanocomposites may serve as promising future bioagents.

candidates.title: Hyaluronic acid-based osmolality-responsive immediate-release microneedles co-loading baicalein and astaxanthin for oral ulcer therapy
candidates.authors: Yang J, Shi K, Wang J, Liu H, Zhang Y, Guang X, Wang S, Lei W, Wang Y, Tan M, Ma X, Wu H
candidates.abstract: Oral ulcers, a prevalent mucosal disorder, are clinically managed by topical corticosteroids and immunosuppressants to alleviate symptoms. However, conventional therapies suffer from suboptimal drug bioavailability, inconsistent efficacy, and potential adverse effects. To address these limitations, using natural carbohydrate polymer hyaluronic acid (HA) with excellent biocompatibility, as the main substrate, we constructed the osmolality-responsive immediate-release microneedles (MNs) platform (GA@BA&Ast MNs) co-loading baicalein (BA) and astaxanthin (Ast) for oral ulcer therapy, which effectively addresses traditional treatment bottlenecks via responsive immediate-release and efficient absorption. The platform's core innovation lies in its dynamically controllable release mechanism, which is triggered specifically by the oral microenvironment. Its osmolality-responsive mechanism, relying on HA-Ca2+ dynamic coordination network dissociation in oral fluid, enables rapid disintegration and delivery speed superior to conventional microneedles, with good mechanical strength for irritation-free mucosal penetration and 85.3%/87.1% cumulative BA/Ast release within 20 min. In the rat model, GA@BA&Ast MNs significantly accelerated ulcer healing, increased collagen deposition and VEGF expression by 41.22% and 47.05%, and exerted complementary antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and ROS scavenging effects by promoting epithelial migration and angiogenesis. This responsive MNs platform overcomes the limitations of hydrophobic drug delivery, providing a promising universal strategy for localized orofacial diseases, such as oral ulcers, oral fibrosis, and oral cancer.

candidates.title: Integrative analysis reveals extensive interactions among C2H2 zinc finger proteins at chromatin loop anchors
candidates.authors: Radovani E, Nabeel-Shah S, Marcon E, Pu S, Zhong G, Tang H, Guo H, Kaplow IM, Emili A, Hughes TR, Greenblatt JF
candidates.abstract: AbstractCys2-His2-zinc-finger proteins (C2H2-ZFPs) form the largest class of human transcription factors, yet their potential roles in higher-order genome organization remain poorly defined. To date, only a few C2H2-ZFPs, e.g. CTCF, have been implicated in chromatin organization. Here, we systematically examined the global relationship between C2H2-ZFPs and long-range chromatin interactions (LRIs). By integrating ChIP-seq datasets for 216 C2H2-ZFPs with genome-wide chromatin interaction maps, we find that >40% of human C2H2-ZFPs are significantly enriched at LRI anchors. Depletion of a subset of such C2H2-ZFPs is associated with altered expression of genes linked by the LRIs they occupy. To investigate whether protein–protein interactions (PPIs) contribute to this pattern, we generated a large-scale interactome using affinity purification-mass spectrometry, encompassing 345 C2H2-ZFPs, and LUMIER binary interaction assays for 204 C2H2-ZFPs, revealing extensive connectivity among the family members. Integrative analysis of PPIs, ChIP-seq, and chromatin interaction datasets revealed that interacting C2H2-ZFP pairs are significantly co-enriched at LRIs and frequently localize to the same or opposing loop anchors. Finally, we show that ∼35% of LRI-associated C2H2-ZFP binding sites overlap somatic mutations in cancer genomes. Together, our results reveal a widespread network of C2H2-ZFP interactions at chromatin loop anchors, providing an important resource for understanding chromatin organization.

candidates.title: Lipid metabolism: a potential checkpoint for cGAS-STING regulation in colorectal cancer
candidates.authors: Qiu Q, Cheng Z, Gu J, Zhang T, Cai M, Wang J
candidates.abstract: Immunotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) continues to face significant challenges, particularly in patients with microsatellite stable (MSS) tumors. The cyclic GMP–AMP synthase–stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS–STING) pathway is a key regulator of innate immunity and has emerged as a promising target for enhancing anti-tumor immune responses. Meanwhile, lipid metabolic reprogramming is a defining hallmark of CRC and contributes to tumor progression, evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Although direct evidence linking lipid metabolism to cGAS–STING signaling in CRC remains limited, accumulating studies from diverse disease models suggest extensive interactions between these two processes. This review summarizes the major features of lipid metabolic reprogramming in CRC and discusses current understanding of cGAS–STING signaling in tumor immunity. We further examine potential mechanisms by which lipid metabolism may influence cGAS–STING activity, including the regulation of mitochondrial DNA release, intracellular trafficking of signaling components and lipid-associated post-translational modifications. Emerging evidence also indicates that cGAS–STING signaling can affect lipid metabolic pathways by regulating lipid metabolic homeostasis and inducing lipid peroxidation-driven ferroptosis. Importantly, microbiota-derived lipid metabolites exert context-dependent effects on cGAS–STING signaling to balance intestinal inflammation and anti-tumor immunity. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism and cGAS–STING signaling, with a particular focus on approaches that may enhance anti-tumor immunity through coordinated metabolic-immune modulation. By bridging metabolic reprogramming with innate immune sensing, we propose that modulating the lipid-cGAS-STING axis could break immune tolerance and offer a distinct therapeutic window for CRC.

candidates.title: Liver enzyme elevations during statin–ezetimibe therapy in ABCG2 c.421C>A variant carriers: a case series and narrative review
candidates.authors: Šimičević L, Ganoci L, Karačić E, Božina T, Pećin I, Trkulja V, Božina N
candidates.abstract: IntroductionStatin–ezetimibe combination therapy is widely used and generally well tolerated; however, liver enzyme elevations may occur during treatment and can be difficult to interpret in patients with polypharmacy and other contributing factors. The potential role of drug–drug–gene interactions (DDGIs) in this context remains insufficiently explored.Materials and MethodsWe present a series of 11 patients from the PGx-CardioDrug study, selected for documented liver enzyme elevations during statin–ezetimibe therapy that led to treatment modification and carriage of the ABCG2 c.421A allele. Clinical characteristics, treatment history, laboratory findings, and outcomes were reviewed alongside available pharmacogenetic results for genes involved in drug transport and metabolism. Available records of five additional ABCG2 c.421CA carriers with documented normal liver enzyme findings during combination therapy were reviewed for descriptive comparison. A narrative review of the literature was conducted to provide a mechanistic interpretation for the observed findings.ResultsThe series included six women and five men, aged 27–78 years. Muscle symptoms and/or creatine kinase (CK) elevations were observed in six patients, including two with rhabdomyolysis requiring hospitalization. Dose reduction, drug discontinuation, or switching to alternative lipid-lowering therapy resulted in improvement of laboratory parameters in several patients. In two patients, abnormalities persisted or increased during subsequent ezetimibe monotherapy. Follow-up laboratory results were not available for all patients. Eight patients had the ABCG2 c.421CA genotype and three had c.421AA, consistent with the selection criterion. Additional findings included variants in SLCO1B1, ABCC2, ABCB1, and UGT1A1. In the five potential comparators, normal liver enzyme findings during combination therapy were supported by numerical laboratory values in three patients and clinical documentation in two.DiscussionThese cases illustrate the difficulty of interpreting liver enzyme elevations during statin–ezetimibe therapy in patients with concomitant medications and other contributing factors. The narrative review provides a pharmacokinetic rationale for considering DDGIs, but the case series does not establish their contribution to the observed abnormalities. Genotype-based selection, incomplete clinical data, and the small descriptive comparator group limit interpretation. These observations remain hypothesis-generating.

candidates.title: Precision in RNA degradation: helicases, ribosome and RNA polymerase stalling, and RNA modifications
candidates.authors: Whisenant DE, Soltys J, Estrella JD, Basu U
candidates.abstract: Errors in transcription and RNA processing generate aberrant transcripts that can produce truncated, nonfunctional, or dominant-negative proteins. RNA surveillance pathways, centered on the RNA exosome, recognize diverse processing defects and initiate targeted RNA degradation. These mechanisms also regulate the short half-life of chromatin-associated noncoding RNAs through co- and/or post-transcriptional degradation. This review examines how the RNA exosome achieves substrate specificity, focusing on its interactions with the helicase cofactors mRNA transport 4 (MTR4) and superkiller 2 (SKIV2L) and the modulatory role of RNA modifications such as N6-methyladenosine. The broad spectrum of RNA exosome targets underscores its central functions in transcription, translation, genome integrity, and cell fate determination.

candidates.title: RNA binding proteome profiling reveals RNA-dependent activation of oncogenic host signaling during KSHV infection
candidates.authors: Zhao Y, Ye X, Yuen M, Zhang R, McDonald WH, Karijolich J
candidates.abstract: Viruses encode RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) to manipulate host processes and promote infection. However, due to limited genomic space, many viral proteins are multifunctional and may engage RNA through non-canonical domains, making their identification difficult using traditional sequence-based approaches. Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) is the etiological agent of many AIDS-associated cancers. Here, leveraging an unbiased proteomic approach we identified all RBPs in KSHV-infected primary effusion lymphoma (PEL) cells, uncovering 7 previously unrecognized KSHV-encoded RBPs. Among these is viral Interferon Regulatory Factor 1 (vIRF1), which we found is both necessary and sufficient to activate oncogenic RAS/MAPK signaling through an RNA-dependent interaction with host G3BP proteins. Importantly, a KSHV vIRF1 mutant lacking the ability to bind RNA exhibits a B cell-specific replication defect, highlighting the essential role of RNA interactions in viral gene regulation and pathogenesis. These findings reveal a novel strategy by which KSHV hijacks RNA-mediated signaling to support its lifecycle.

candidates.title: Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Signaling in Mammalian Eye Development
candidates.authors: Makrides N, Wu Y, Almonte Y, Zhang X, Tao C
candidates.abstract: Receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling is a central mechanism by which local tissue interactions are translated into coordinated morphogenesis during eye development. The vertebrate eye provides a uniquely tractable system for studying this logic because it is assembled from neural epithelium, surface ectoderm, neural crest–derived mesenchyme, vascular endothelium, and specialized epithelial and endothelial derivatives across a prolonged developmental timeline. In this review, we synthesize how major RTK families, including FGF–FGFR, EGF-ErbB, PDGF–PDGFR, VEGF–VEGFR, Eph-ephrin, ANGPT–TEK/Tie2, IGF-INS receptors, and collagen-sensing DDRs, control optic cup formation, optic fissure closure, lens differentiation and architecture, corneal and anterior segment morphogenesis, retinal vascularization, Schlemm’s canal development, and lacrimal gland branching. Rather than acting through pathway-specific outputs, these receptors repeatedly converge on shared MAPK/ERK, PI3K–AKT, PLCγ–PKC, SRC/FAK, and Rho-family cytoskeletal modules. Developmental specificity emerges from ligand geography, receptor dosage, co-receptor and extracellular matrix context, signal duration, receptor trafficking, mechanical state, and cross-talk with other signaling pathways. We also highlight how emerging single-cell, spatial, and multiomic atlases are shifting the field from static expression maps toward ligand–receptor source mapping and quantitative pathway-state inference. Finally, we connect developmental RTK mechanisms to congenital and pediatric eye disease. Together, these studies position the eye as a powerful model for understanding how reiterative RTK signaling builds complex organ form and informs therapeutic modulation, regenerative medicine, and disease mechanism.

candidates.title: SNOOPPI: a sequence-normalized database of on- and off-target protein–protein interactions
candidates.authors: Vincoff S, Chatterjee P
candidates.abstract: AbstractMotivationProtein–protein interactions (PPIs) are central to biological processes and therapeutic interventions. While many databases document known PPIs, these resources often lack evidence-based negatives and clear identification of the specific proteoforms tested.ResultsHere, we introduce SNOOPPI, a Sequence-Normalized database of on- and off-target protein–protein interactions, which represents the first unified dataset of binary PPIs that is isoform, post-translational modification, mutation, and binding site aware. By defining a PPI as a direct, physical interaction between two amino acid sequences, SNOOPPI overcomes several persistent limitations of existing PPI databases. SNOOPPI was curated from the IntAct database, taking full advantage of its experimental metadata and feature annotations to reclassify and uncover new PPIs. The final dataset comprises over 33.6K positive interactions and 5.3K negative interactions. SNOOPPI also retains over 835K unresolved interactions, explicitly capturing gaps in the experimental literature. Beyond its usefulness as a reference dataset for the scientific community, SNOOPPI has the potential to serve as a high-confidence foundation for sequence-based modeling, benchmarking, and generative design of novel protein and peptide interactors.Availability and implementationThe full database can be accessed and downloaded through an interactive Hugging Face page: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ChatterjeeLab/SNOOPPI. All code is open-source and maintained at https://github.com/sophievincoff/snooppi. The database and associated code will be updated periodically to incorporate new IntAct releases. The specific version of the code associated with this publication is archived at the following Zenodo repository: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22116350.

candidates.title: Snapshots of internal protein crystal architecture at the nanoscale
candidates.authors: Nia SS, Saha A, Cho J, Zhou ZH, Ercius P, Mecklenburg M
candidates.abstract: Macromolecular crystallography has historically inferred models of internal crystal architecture from reciprocal-space measurements of Bragg reflections. Nevertheless, direct real-space visualization of crystallographic disorder remains elusive, particularly at the nanoscale. Using a 15-nm probe, here we apply both ambient-temperature and cryogenic four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) to map the topography of coherently diffracting domains (CDDs) in lysozyme and myoglobin microcrystals at length scales 100× finer than conventional X-ray and electron beams. Virtual dark-field images show that each Bragg peak arises from spatially distinct subvolumes representing smooth and continuous variations in local lattice orientation. Under sustained irradiation, protein CDDs undergo rearrangements spanning several micrometers of internal movement. Furthermore, pinpoint high-dose “impact crater” experiments reveal delocalized radiolytic damage propagating hundreds of nanometers from primary irradiation sites, behavior similar to small-molecule crystals but amplified in both rate and magnitude. Together, these results establish macromolecular microcrystals as dynamic assemblies whose internal architecture continuously reorganizes during irradiation, laying the foundation for realistic models of mosaicity directly informed by both real-space and reciprocal-space observations.

candidates.title: StrucNS reveals interaction-weighted network topology as the driving predictor of absolute stability of natural and de novo proteins
candidates.authors: Mullick A, Daoutidis P, Hackel BJ
candidates.abstract: AbstractMotivationFolded protein function requires stability, yet mapping structure and sequence to a fitness landscape remains difficult. The protein fold is the physical realization of complex, spatially-sensitive physicochemical interactions; quantitatively elucidating how these subtle relationships dictate thermodynamic stability remains challenging. We present StrucNS, a mathematical framework that identifies principles governing protein fitness by employing network science to learn physicochemical relationships between residues and their stability contributions directly from the protein fold. While the fold is traditionally viewed as the phenotypic consequence of the underlying chemical forces, we represent the fold as a network topology to decode the physicochemical dependencies that govern protein stability. Unlike language models reliant on high-dimensional evolutionary embeddings, StrucNS extracts these signals directly from the interaction-weighted network topology. Evolutionary independence uniquely suits StrucNS for de novo design prediction.ResultsDespite reduced dimensionality and training depth, StrucNS outperforms unsupervised ESM-2 and ProteinMPNN on predicting mutational stability across three miniprotein test sets. StrucNS performs comparably to supervised UniRep in predicting absolute stability of de novo designs and outperforms supervised UniRep and supervised ESM-2 in predicting mutational stability of multi-mutants far outside its training regime. Feature analysis reveals network topology drive predictive power. SHAP analysis reveals high degree and low modularity of polar/hydrophobic mixed subnetworks as influential features, which highlights connectivity between the hydrophobic core and protein surface as predictive of stability contrary to the conventional focus on the hydrophobic core. Revelation of predictive topological features underscores the utility of interpretability.AvailabilitySource codes and datasets: https://github.com/Hackel-Group-CEMS/StrucNS and https://zenodo.org/records/20497907.

candidates.title: The chromosome-level genome of Mesobuthus martensii provides insights into its evolution and the diversity of venom peptides
candidates.authors: Liu D, Zeng Q, Sun Y, Li C, Song Y, Shang Z, Li K, Zhu H, Li F, Shen C, Ju J
candidates.abstract: Mesobuthus martensii, the source species of the traditional Chinese medicine “Quanxie”, has long been utilized for its therapeutic properties. Venom peptides are recognized as the major active molecular basis of these pharmacological activities. Despite this, their development as therapeutic agents remains poorly explored. In this study, we performed an integrated multi-omics investigation to systematically explore the venom peptides of Mesobuthus martensii. We generated a chromosome-level genome assembly of Mesobuthus martensii using third-generation sequencing technologies, yielding a genome size of 1.08 Gb with a contig N50 of 46.46 Mb. Integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses led to the identification of 51 putative novel venom peptide candidates. From the broader venom peptide set, five lysine- and arginine-rich candidates were selected for recombinant expression and functional characterization. Functional evaluation revealed that MmTX67, MmTX106 and MmTX126 modulated coagulation-related parameters in vitro, with MmTX106 further demonstrating the most pronounced antithrombotic effect in vivo. Collectively, these findings provide novel insights into the genetic basis of bioactive substances in “Quanxie” and highlight MmTX106 as the most promising antithrombotic candidate, while providing a molecular foundation for further evaluation of other scorpion venom-derived peptide candidates.
